# Page 19^page=19
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 19 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS Overview of Bharat Tribes Fest 2026 Held in New Delhi The Bharat Tribes Fest (BTF 2026), a national celebration of tribal culture, craftsmanship, and entrepreneurship, was held from March 18 to April 5, 2026 at Sunder Nursery, New Delhi (Delhi). • The festival served as a platform to bridge the gap between traditional tribal artisans and modern global markets. Exam Hints: ✓ Event: BTF 2026 ✓ Duration: March 18 to April 05, 2026 ✓ Organised by: MoTA and TRIFED ✓ Inaugurated by: Union Minister Jual Oram, MoTA ✓ Key Launch: ‘RISA: Timeless Tribal Brand’ ✓ Phase-I: 10 clusters covering 5 tribal weaves, 2 embroideries and 3 crafts ✓ Other Key Conclaves: Bharat Tribes Business Conclave, CSR Conclave, and Van Dhan Conclave ✓ Outcome: Rs.4.5 crore sales. About BTF 2026: Organiser: The 19-day long event was organized by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) in association with the Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India (TRIFED). Opening Ceremony: The festival was inaugurated by Union Minister Jual Oram, MoTA, in the presence of Dao Ngoc Dung, Minister of Ethnic and Religious Affairs, and Y. Thong, Vice Minister of Ethnic and Religious Affairs from the Socialist Republic of Vietnam. Key Dignitaries: Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, MoTA; M. Rajamurugan, Managing Director (MD), TRIFED; Manish Thakur, Additional Secretary, MoTA and senior officials, tribal leaders, artisans, and other stakeholders, were present at the event. Key Participants: The event witnessed the participation of more than 300 art and craft participants from across the country. Also, 120 tribal cuisine participants presented authentic regional dishes and 400+ tribal artists performing traditional dances and music. Key Demonstrations: The festival featured over 200 curated stalls showcasing tribal products; about 75 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) promoting value-added forest produce; 17 live craft demonstrations by master artisans. Launch of RISA: Launch: During the event, Union Minister Jual Oram launched ‘RISA: Timeless Tribal’, an exclusive signature brand dedicated to tribal weaves and crafts. The name is inspired by Tripura’s traditional handwoven stole, the Risa. Aim: To preserve tribal looms and craft traditions, and to draw focus and generate interest among discerning consumers towards tribal fabric/apparel, embroideries and handicrafts. Key Features: The new initiative includes the creation of new designs for tribal weaves, embroideries, and handicrafts and produce newer products thereafter; training and capacity building of tribal weavers and artisans and development of weaving and handicraft clusters. Premium Packaging: The National Institute of Design (NID) Haryana has developed sustainable, eco-friendly premium packaging for the custom-tailored segment.

# Page 20^page=20
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 20 Daily Content PDF Design Partnerships: The product launch revolves around Strategic Partnerships with renowned fashion designers including Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla, Manish Tripathi, Anju Modi, Gaurav Jai Gupta, among others. Implementation: In the first phase the project features 10 clusters covering 5 tribal weaves, 2 embroideries and 3 crafts. • The first phase of the RISA features a curated selection of some of India’s most iconic weaves and crafts, including Eri Silk (Bodo community in Assam), Santal Cotton (Santal community in Jharkhand), Changpa Pashmina (Changpa community in Ladakh), Kotpad Cotton (Mirgan community in Odisha), Muga Silk (Miri community in Assam), Dongria embroidery (Dongria Kondh community in Odisha), and Toda embroidery (Toda community in Tamil Nadu, TN). • Besides, the brand will also showcase specialized Handicrafts including Longpi Pottery (Manipur), Turtuk Brass Cutlery (Ladakh), and the world-renowned Dokhra Art (Chhattisgarh). Highlights of BTF 2026: Key Conclaves: The fest hosted various conclaves including, Bharat Tribes Business Conclave, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Conclave, and Van Dhan Conclave, which brought together policymakers, industry leaders, corporates, and community stakeholders to deliberate on issues such as market access, branding, innovation, and sustainable livelihoods. • TRIFED organised a Van Dhan Conclave which featured 5 thematic sessions focusing on sustainable livelihoods, value addition of Minor Forest Produce, market linkages, and strengthening tribal entrepreneurship. • The fest also witnessed the inauguration of the Signature Pavilion, displaying curated tribal textiles and crafts developed through collaborations between leading designers and tribal artisans. Awards/Honors: At the end of the fest, top-performing tribal artisans and sellers across 10 categories including, Pottery, Cane & Bamboo, Jewellery, Cuisines, Gifts & Assortments, Metal, Naturals, Paintings, Textiles, and VDVKs, were felicitated by M. Rajamurugan, MD of TRIFED, and Anant Prakash Pandey, Joint Secretary, MoTA, in the presence of dignitaries and stakeholders. Outcome: The festival attracted over 1.50 lakh visitors and generated Rs.4.5 crore in sales, reflecting the growing demand for tribal products. About Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA): Union Minister – Jual Oram (Constituency – Sundargarh, Odisha) Minister of State (MoS) – Durga Das Uikey (Constituency – Betul, Madhya Pradesh, MP) MIB Notifies TV Rating Policy 2026 to Enhance Transparency, Accountability & Credibility In April 2026, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB) notified the ‘Television (TV) Rating Policy (TRP 2026)’, replacing the existing 2014 guidelines TV governing audience measurement in India. • This move aims to enhance transparency, accountability and credibility in India’s TV audience measurement. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Notification of Television Rating Policy (TRP 2026) ✓ Issued by: MIB ✓ Replaces: 2014 TRP Guidelines ✓ Purpose: To enhance transparency, Credibility and Accountability in TV audience measurement

# Page 21^page=21
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 21 Daily Content PDF ✓ Key Provisions: ✓ Net Worth: Reduced to Rs.5 crore (from Rs.20 crore) ✓ Sample Size: 80,000 metered homes (target: 1.2 lakh) ✓ Coverage: Cable, DTH, OTT & connected TVs ✓ Governance: 50% independent directors ✓ Compliance: DPDP Act, 2023 ✓ Grievance: Nodal officer (10-day resolution). Key Reforms in TRP Guidelines 2026: Viewership: As per TRP 2026, any viewership arising out of landing page will be excluded in viewership measurement Governance Norms: The policy mandates that at least 50% of the Board must be independent directors with no links to broadcasters or advertisers, and prohibits consultancy roles to prevent conflicts of interest. Net-Worth: MIB has eased the minimum net worth requirement for a company willing to register as TV rating agency from existing Rs 20 crore to Rs.5 crore. Sample Size: As per the notification, TV rating agencies are now required to scale up their operations to 80,000 metered(m) homes within 18 months (6 months for existing rating agencies), with a long-term goal of 1.20 lakh homes. Technology-Neutral Measurement: The ratings measurement will now include viewership from cable, Direct-to-Home (DTH), Over The Top (OTT) platforms and connected TVs. • MIB has further clarified that data shall be captured from all the TV viewing screens of the metered homes. Measures to Enhance Transparency: Rating Agencies have been mandated to disclose their methodologies and publish anonymised data on their websites, ensuring transparency in capturing TRP. Dual-Audit System: It is now mandatory for TV rating agencies to implement a dual-audit system, featuring quarterly internal audits and annual independent external audits, aimed to improve data accuracy and integrity. • Also, MIB has proposed to form an Audit & Oversight team for periodic field inspections. Data Privacy & Penalties: Also, all operations must strictly comply with the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP Act, 2023), ensuring viewer privacy. • MIB has clarified that non-compliance with new TRP regulations will attract penalties like: temporary suspensions of ratings to the cancellation of registration for repeat violations. Grievance Redressal Mechanism: MIB has mandated all the rating agencies to appoint a nodal officer to resolve complaints within 10 days and set up an Appellate Authority for escalated disputes. About Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB): Union Minister- Ashwini Vaishnaw (Rajya Sabha member- Odisha) Minister of State (MoS)- Loganathan Murugan (Rajya Sabha member- Madhya Pradesh, MP) Union MoS Dr. Jitendra Singh Launches first -ever ‘Administrative Capacity Building’ Programme for Scientists & Academicians In April 2026, Union Minister of State (MoS) (Independent Charge, IC) Dr. Jitendra Singh, Ministry of Science and Technology (MoS&T), launched the first-ever dedicated programme on ‘Administrative Capacity Building for Scientists and Academicians’ under Mission Karmayogi, during a special session of ‘SADHANA(Strengthening Adaptive Development and Humane Aptitude for National Advancement) Saptah’ held at Vigyan Bhawan in New Delhi, Delhi. • This newly launched initiative aims to equip scientists and academic leaders with governance skills and decision-making capabilities.

# Page 24^page=24
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 24 Daily Content PDF ECONOMY & BUSINESS Moody’s Lowers India’s FY27 GDP Growth Forecast to 6% Amid West Asia Conflict In April 2026, American rating agency, Moody’s Ratings released its latest ‘Credit Opinion Report on India’, lowering India’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth forecast for Financial Year 2026-27(FY27) by 80 basis points to 6%, down from its earlier estimate of 6.8%. • The report further cautioned about ongoing conflict in West Asia which is expected to moderate growth momentum and raise inflation risks. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Moody’s lowers India’s GDP forecast for FY27 ✓ India’s Revised GDP: 6% (-80 bps) ✓ Key Reason: Inflation Risks Emerging from West Asia Conflict ✓ Growth Trend: 7.5% (CY25) vs 7.2% (CY24) ✓ Inflation: 4.8% (in FY27) ✓ CAD: 1-1.5% of GDP (CY26 and CY27). Key Findings: Growth Trend: Moody’s noted that India’s GDP growth remained strong at 7.5% in Calendar Year 2025(CY25), up from 7.2% in CY24, driven by a rebound in the manufacturing sector. Key Contributors: The report outlined key contributors for downward growth projections: weaker private consumption, softer industrial activity, among others. Debt Consolidation: Despite emerging fiscal risks due to West Asia conflict, the report expected gradual debt consolidation in line with the Government of India (GoI)’s medium-term objective of reducing central government debt to nearly 50% of GDP by FY31, from around 57% of GDP in FY25. Inflation: The rating has also projected inflation to average at 4.8% in FY27 from 2.4% in FY26. Fiscal Indicators: The report highlighted India’s Current Account Deficit (CAD) narrowed to nearly 0.4% of GDP in CY25 over 0.9% (in CY24). • The report further estimated India’s CAD to remain around 1-1.5% of GDP in CY26 and CY27. Export & Import: The report noted that stable external position is mainly due to gradual increase in goods exports offset by high goods imports, particularly in imported fuels and raw materials. • Further, goods and services exports are expected to remain stable, even as goods imports will expand due to higher global commodity prices, depending on the duration of ongoing conflict in West Asia. About Moody’s Ratings: President- Michael West Headquarters- New York, the United States of America (USA) Founded- 1909 APPOINTMENTS & RESIGNATIONS Croatian High Jumper ‘Blanka Vlašić’ Appointed International Event Ambassador for TCS World 10K Bengaluru 2026 In April 2026, Procam International, a sports management company in India, announced that Croatian high jumper and double Olympic medallist Blanka Vlašić has been appointed as the International Event Ambassador for the 18th edition of the Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) World 10K Bengaluru.

# Page 26^page=26
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 26 Daily Content PDF IMPORTANT DAYS National Maritime Day 2026 – April 5 National Maritime Day (NMD) is observed annually in India on April 5 to celebrate the country’s maritime heritage and recognize the vital role of the shipping sector in trade, connectivity, and national development. • 5th April 2026 marks the 63rd observance of the NMD • The day commemorates the 1919 maiden voyage of SS Loyalty, India’s first Swadeshi ship operated by the Scindia Steam Navigation Company Limited, from Mumbai (Maharashtra) to London on April 5, 1919, marking India’s entry into global shipping. Theme: 2026 Theme: “Maritime India – Empowering Progress.” Focus: The theme focuses on strengthening maritime infrastructure, promoting sustainability, and driving economic growth. Exam Hints: ✓ What? National Maritime Day 2026 ✓ When? April 5 ✓ 2026 Observance: 63rd ✓ 2026 theme: “Maritime India – Empowering Progress” ✓ Maritime Week 2026: Observed from 29 March to 5 April 2026 ✓ 1st observance: 5 April 1964 ✓ Purpose: Commemorates SS Loyalty voyage (1919) ✓ 2026 Event: Secretary of MoPSW Vijay Kumar pinned the Merchant Navy flag on PM Narendra Modi March 31, 2026. Background: Origin: NMD was initiated by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping, and Waterways (MoPSW). First Observance: The first NMD was observed on 5 April 1964. Maritime Week 2026: Observance: National Maritime Week 2026 in India, also known as Merchant Navy Week, was observed from 29 March to 5 April 2026, culminating in the 63rd NMD. 2026 Events: Ceremonial Launch: Vijay Kumar, Secretary of the MoPSW, ceremonially pinned the Merchant Navy Miniature Flag/National Maritime Day Celebrations (NMDC) lapel pin on Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi on 31 March 2026, marking the commencement of Merchant Navy Week. • The same ceremonial gesture was extended to President Droupadi Murmu, signifying the national-level inauguration of the celebrations. Launch: This “Flag Pinning” tradition serves as the formal launch of National Maritime Week (Merchant Navy Week), leading up to National Maritime Day on 5 April. Symbolism: The gesture represents national recognition of seafarers’ dedication and highlights the maritime sector’s vital role in India’s global trade, economic growth, and strategic sovereignty. Ports: Major events were conducted at key ports including Mumbai (Maharashtra), Chennai (Tamil Nadu, TN), Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh, AP), and Kolkata (West Bengal, WB). About Sagar Samman Awards: Overview: As part of the NMD celebrations, the MoPSW annually presents the Sagar Samman Awards to recognise individuals and organisations for their exemplary contributions to the maritime sector. The awards are categorised as follows:

# Page 27^page=27
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 27 Daily Content PDF • Varuna Award: The highest honor granted for consistently exceptional leadership contributions and includes a statue of Lord Varuna, a certificate, and a citation. • Award for Excellence: The second highest recognizes meritorious contributions of a very high order and includes a ship model, certificate, and citation. • Award for Gallantry: Recognizes exceptional acts of bravery in maritime situations. India’s Maritime Sector: Trade: Over 90% of India’s trade by volume is transported via sea routes, supported by a coastline exceeding 7,500 kilometer (km) and a network of 12 major ports and over 200 non-major ports, underscoring its importance to global supply chains, energy security, and geopolitical stability. Infrastructure: Port infrastructure is being expanded under the Sagarmala Programme (launched by the MoPSW in 2015) to enhance capacity and reduce vessel turnaround time from 93 hours to 48 hours. Development: The Blue Economy is being promoted as a major contributor to India’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and employment, alongside sustainability efforts such as Green Ports, alternative fuels like hydrogen and ammonia, and the strengthening of the SAGAR Initiative (Security and Growth for All in the Region) for regional security. About Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW): Union Minister – Sarbananda Sonowal (Constituency – Dibrugarh, Assam) Minister of State (MoS) – Shantanu Thakur (Constituency – Bangaon, West Bengal, WB) International Day of Sport for Development and Peace 2026 – April 6 The United Nations (UN’s) International Day of Sport for Development and Peace (IDSDP) is observed annually across the globe on April 6 to highlight the role of sport in promoting peace, inclusion, human rights, and sustainable development. • 6th April 2026 marks the 13th observance of IDSDP.
